 Hon'Ble Krishan Pahal, J.
1. List has been revised.
2. Supplementary affidavit filed today is taken on record.

3. Heard Sri Hari Nath Chaubey, learned counsel for applicant, Ms. Ifra Islam, learned State Law Officer for the State and perused the material placed on record.
4.

The present bail application has been filed by the applicant in Case Crime No.23 of 2024, under Sections 498A, 304B and 201 I.P.C. and Section 3/4 D.P. Act, Police Station-Reuna, District-Kanpur Nagar with the prayer to enlarge him on bail.
5. As per the certificate regarding compliance of the order of this Court dated 26.08.2025, the cost has been deposited.
6. Learned counsel for the applicant has stated that the FIR is delayed by about three days and there is no explanation of the said delay caused.
The dead body of the deceased was recovered from River Yamuna and cause of death could not be ascertained, as such, Viscera was preserved.
The Viscera report is still awaited.
It is a blind murder and the applicant has nothing to do with the said offence.

7. Learned counsel for the applicant further stated that statement of P.W.1, who is the father of the deceased person, was recorded and he has not supported the prosecution story to the extent that no dowry was demanded.
Statement of P.W.2, who is the mother of the deceased person, was recorded and she has not supported the prosecution story and has been declared hostile.
It is further argued that brother of the deceased is being examined today in trial court concerned.

It is also argued that sister of the deceased, with whom the applicant is stated to have established illicit relationship, was also made an accused and she has been granted bail by co-ordinate Bench of this Court vide order dated 03.07.2024.
There is no criminal history of the applicant.
The applicant is in jail since 10.02.2024 and he is ready to cooperate with trial.
In case, the applicant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail.

8. Per contra, learned State Law Officer has vehemently opposed the bail application on the ground that applicant did not even inform anybody about the missing of his wife and he did not file any missing report at the police station which indicates that he was involved in the said offence, as such,
he is not entitled for bail.
9.
This Court had called for status of trial from the trial court concerned.

As per the status report dated 08.08.2025 received from the trial court concerned, six witnesses have been examined during Shailendra @ Shailesh vs State Of U.P. on 3 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/138365990/

sentences.text: The bail should not be normally granted to the accused after the charge has been framed.
It should also not be granted by looking into the discrepancies here or there in the deposition.

11. After hearing learned counsel for the parties and taking into consideration the fact that six witnesses have been examined during trial and trial is at its conclusive end coupled with the fact that applicant did not move any application about the missing of his wife, I do not find it a fit case for grant of bail to the applicant.
12. The bail application is found devoid of merits and is, accordingly, rejected.

13. However, it is directed that the aforesaid case pending before the trial court be decided expeditiously in view of the principle as has been laid down in the recent judgments of the Supreme Court in the cases of Vinod Kumar vs. State of Punjab; 2015 (3) SCC 220 and Hussain and Another vs. Union of India; (2017) 5 SCC 702, if there is no legal impediment.
